g.title: note
g.text: Historical reference: Jan Engelhardt, 2014-Feb-28, Linux 2.6.36+ (not all Linux 2.x).
Re-drawn stage model, not copied SVG artwork. Blue: bridge/L2; orange: IPv4 hooks; green/purple: modern extensions.
Priority is per-hook, lower runs earlier. raw_before_defrag may move raw to -450.
NAT rules normally see the first connection packet; conntrack applies subsequent translations.
MODERN Netfilter BPF may attach inside IPv4 hooks at configured priority (since 6.4).
iptables -m bpf runs BPF within a rule match (xt_bpf); not a separate Netfilter hook.
Bridge NF_BR_* and IPv4 NF_INET_* are distinct hook families. XFRM arrows summarize mode-dependent paths.
ARP/IPv6/hardware offload details excluded. Every hook can terminate/divert a packet.

g.title: matrix
g.text: IPv4 iptables-legacy: four tables / five chains
Optional security table: INPUT / FORWARD / OUTPUT at +50
INPUT nat exists since 2.6.36. raw_before_defrag may use -450.

g.title: comparison
g.text: named tables; base chain specifies type / hook / priority
nft sets/maps and atomic batch updates; ip/inet/bridge/netdev families
Shared hook: callbacks ordered by priority, NOT legacy then nft.
ACCEPT in one base chain does not skip later chains; DROP terminates.
Stateful NAT normally evaluates rules for the first connection packet.
Netfilter BPF: callback in hook; xt_bpf: match within an iptables rule.
